benchmark_explanation: This instance uses 4.20/4.7.2 B60-prefix nested scaling: B120 is a prefix of one deterministic B360 common-pool append stream, not a freshly regenerated B120 instance.
The common-pool RNG seed is 161262537; when this is set to the verified B120 seed 161262537, increasing pool_blocks preserves the successful B120 prefix while extending the same append stream.
The first 60 recourse blocks are byte-identical to the B60-good seed8 instance, and the first-stage capacity domain is frozen at U=(6,6,6) before applying the tail-continuous adapter.
This isolates scaling in the decomposable recourse side while preserving the B60 first-stage geometry, tail_start, and z-domain after tail-cont lifting.
The tail-continuous variant keeps the original integer capacity lattice as the main structure but adds a very small continuous flexibility interval at the highest capacity level.
Because u_i appears in Bz through zcap_i=y_i+u_i, a fixed-z enumerator cannot fully remove the global z coupling when a tail mode is active.
This run is a transparent homogeneous-A0 benchmark, not the original heterogeneous instance.
generator_notes: 4.20/4.7.2 NestedB60 enabled: B120 is the first 120 blocks of the deterministic B360 common-pool append stream built from the B60-good seed8 prefix.
Append strategy used = common_pool; this reuses profile-preserving perturbed-copy expansion but removes target-dependent append streams, so the requested target sizes are truly nested.
Common-pool RNG seed used = 161262537; default seed for this pool would be 11362844; override active = 1.
Frozen first-stage domain verified before tail-cont: U=(6,6,6); only the number of recourse blocks changes.

dcap_like_sun prefix expansion is enabled: first 60 x-blocks are the exact original generated B60 seed8 instance; blocks 61-120 are deterministic profile-preserving perturbed copies of those base blocks.
This is an instance-layer scaling option only. It does not modify P1/P2, the inner oracle, the Pessoa outer state machine, rho policy, LB/UB certificate, or final stopping logic.
The expansion isolates the effect of increasing decomposable x-block count while keeping z dimension, tier capacities/costs, budget, base task sizes/values, and the original hard B60 prefix fixed.
Perturbation jitter for appended blocks is 0.0200; setting --dcap_expand_jitter 0 creates exact repeated copies.

Expansion RNG seed used for appended blocks is 161262537; for B60/B120 this remains the original default stream; seed1 B80 keeps its previous tuned stream, and seed1 B100 is retuned to extend that same B80-good appended-block stream.
dcap_like_sun is a transparent, documented DCAP-like Sun benchmark family rather than a claim of exact SIPLIB/DCAP generator replication.

Its semantics follow the public DCAP skeleton: first-stage binary tier activations buy coarse resource-period capacity, while each local x-block solves a recourse assignment of realized task demand to purchased capacity under scenario-specific processing requirements.

Its structure follows Sun: z is a mild central coordination layer with resource-family × coarse-period × tier binaries, x = (x^1, ..., x^P) consists of many local recourse blocks, and all x-blocks decompose naturally once z is fixed.

The benchmark search is purely structural and reproducible from instance_seed; it never uses P1/P2/Gurobi outcomes. The active dcap_gurobi_profile is 'seed159_sunint_dz3_u6_tail48'; the seed159 profiles target a Gurobi-facing sweet spot with material but not maximal disagreement.
The search examined 1 candidate draws derived from instance_seed=8 and selected attempt 1 with sweet-spot score 5.4435.
The realized mild-z design uses 3 first-stage binaries (1 periods × 3 resource families × 1 tiers) and 60 local x-blocks.

The profile mix intentionally keeps a balanced-block majority while retaining early-focus, late-focus, and a small split-focus minority, so the family preserves competing pulls on z without forcing maximal local disagreement everywhere.

The realized z choice mode is 'integer_capacity' and the block weight mode is 'unit'. In EF-hard mode this is intentionally used to keep the z-pattern count small while making the x-side extensive form large.
[Dz3MildZ] true_grid_size=343 true_feasible_count=122 budget=88 u_cap=6 capacity_scale=2.5
The legacy CSV field n_scenarios is kept for backward compatibility; in dcap_like_sun it should be interpreted as the number of x-blocks / scenarios in the Sun-style block-angular family.
4.19 masked tail-continuous DCAP adapter enabled: original z dimension 3 is kept in a y/b/u layout of dimension 9; active tail dims = (1,).
Only active u_i coordinates enter Bz and first-stage cost; inactive u_i are fixed at zero while their y_i/b_i variables preserve the original integer levels 0..U_i.
Tail domain has Delta=0.1; tail starts are (6.0, 6.0, 6.0); RNC tail-u distance scale is 0.001.
Homogeneous common-technology variant: every local coupling matrix A_p is replaced by A_0 after nested and continuous-tail construction.
All algorithms, residual calculations, fixed-z audits, and the Gurobi extensive form use the same transformed instance.
Explicit candidate override: family seed=8, candidate index=9, candidate seed=1373808879.

family_payload.dcap_nested_b60_note: 4.7.2 nested B60 scaling: target instance is the first B blocks of one deterministic B60-to-pool common pool; the B60 first-stage domain is frozen before the tail-cont adapter.
